questions.q: What is the main difference between a numpy array and a pandas Series?
options: A Series has an index of labels
A Series can hold only text
why: Correct. Labels let pandas match data by label.
A Series holds numbers, text, dates and more.
Speed is similar. The labels are the difference.

questions.q: s = pd.Series([10, 20, 30], index=[5, 6, 7]). What is s.iloc[0]?
questions.why: iloc uses positions. Position 0 is the first value, 10. (s.loc[5] gives the same value.)

questions.q: a = pd.Series([1, 2, 3], index=[0, 1, 2]) and b = pd.Series([10, 20, 30], index=[1, 2, 3]). What is (a + b).loc[2]?
questions.why: Label 2 is in both. a has 3 and b has 20, so the sum is 23. Position does not matter.

questions.q: With the same a and b, how many values does a.add(b, fill_value=0) have?
questions.why: The result index is the union of [0,1,2] and [1,2,3], which is [0,1,2,3]. That makes 4 values, with no NaN.

questions.q: You join two daily series. One misses 3 days. You see 3 NaN. Reports from a missing day mean 'zero sales'. Which fix is right?
why: Correct. A missing report means zero, so 0 is the honest fill.
This loses the days, so the series has holes.
A mean invents sales on days with no report.

questions.q: Which expression selects rows where units is above 10 and returns only the column revenue?
why: Correct. The first part filters rows, the second picks the column.
iloc needs positions, not a boolean Series with labels.

questions.q: Which call counts the missing values in a Series s?
why: Correct. isna gives True for missing, and the sum counts them.
